mechanicLegendsCodes.title: Mechanic Legends Codes
mechanicLegendsCodes.subtitle: Check available redemption information, rewards, and the correct way to enter codes in Mechanic Legends.
mechanicLegendsCodes.intro: Mechanic Legends codes can provide useful bonuses such as Cash, Spins, or other in-game rewards. Open the game, locate the code interface, enter each code exactly as displayed, and redeem it before the code expires.

items.reward: Cash, Spins, or promotional rewards when an active code is available
items.details: Enter codes exactly as provided, including capitalization and numbers. A code can only be redeemed when the developer has enabled it.

items.reward: Applies the reward attached to a valid code
items.details: Launch Mechanic Legends, enter the garage or main interface, open the Codes or gift-code option, type the code into the input field, and select Redeem.

items.reward: No reward is granted until the code is accepted
items.details: Common causes include an expired promotion, incorrect capitalization, extra spaces, a code already redeemed on the account, or entering the code in the wrong interface.

mechanicLegendsBeginnerGuide.title: Mechanic Legends Beginner Guide
mechanicLegendsBeginnerGuide.subtitle: Start Strong in Mechanic Legends: follow a practical garage-to-road progression covering vehicles, repairs, upgrades, jobs, and activities.
mechanicLegendsBeginnerGuide.intro: New players should first learn the garage interface and basic vehicle controls before spending heavily on upgrades. A steady progression of repairs, jobs, and carefully chosen improvements provides the resources needed to unlock better vehicles and more profitable activities.

steps.title: Enter the garage and learn the controls
steps.description: Start in the garage, inspect the available interaction points, and learn how to move between the vehicle, repair area, dealership, and activity locations.

steps.title: Choose an affordable starter vehicle
steps.description: Purchase a vehicle that fits the starting budget and keep enough Cash available for repairs and essential improvements instead of spending the entire balance immediately.

steps.title: Repair the vehicle before upgrading it
steps.description: Restore the vehicle to a usable condition before investing in performance parts. A damaged vehicle can reduce efficiency and make early activities harder to complete.

steps.title: Complete beginner-friendly work
steps.description: Use available jobs, deliveries, or other low-risk activities to build Cash. Focus on consistent completion rather than expensive upgrades during the first stage.

steps.title: Upgrade for the activities you play
steps.description: Improve handling, acceleration, durability, or other relevant attributes according to your preferred activity. Avoid buying parts that do not improve your current route.

steps.title: Expand into events and better vehicles
steps.description: Once the vehicle is repaired and the garage has a stable income flow, try racing and other activities, then save toward vehicles with stronger performance or broader utility.

mechanicLegendsMoneyMaking.title: Mechanic Legends Money Making Guide
mechanicLegendsMoneyMaking.subtitle: Best Ways to Make Money: compare repairs, jobs, deliveries, taxi work, and racing to choose an income route for every stage of progression.
mechanicLegendsMoneyMaking.intro: The best money-making activity depends on the vehicle you own, the amount of Cash available for repairs, and how confidently you can complete the activity. Start with steady work, reinvest selectively, and move into faster or more demanding activities as your vehicle improves.

items.strategy: Prioritize repair work when you need predictable income and are still learning the garage systems. Keep repair expenses under control so the activity remains profitable.
Use regular jobs to build a steady Cash reserve before purchasing expensive vehicles or performance parts.
Choose deliveries that fit the vehicle's condition and travel ability. Efficient routing reduces downtime between rewards.
Taxi work becomes more practical after the vehicle is dependable and can handle repeated trips without frequent repair interruptions.
Race after investing in suitable performance and handling improvements. Racing offers stronger upside but is less predictable when the vehicle is underpowered or difficult to control.

mechanicLegendsCarsDealership.title: Mechanic Legends Cars and Dealership Guide
mechanicLegendsCarsDealership.subtitle: Choose the Right Car for Every Activity: understand vehicle roles, dealership purchases, and how to match a car's strengths to repairs, deliveries, taxi work, and racing.
mechanicLegendsCarsDealership.intro: Vehicle selection in Mechanic Legends is about balancing purchase cost, current condition, performance, and intended use. A practical collection can include a steady everyday vehicle, a work-focused vehicle, and a faster option for competitive activities.

items.buyingGuidance: Choose an affordable vehicle that leaves enough Cash for repairs and basic upgrades. Dependability is more valuable than peak performance during the opening stage.
Favor vehicles that remain dependable over multiple trips. A balanced setup reduces downtime and makes recurring work more consistent.
Purchase a performance-focused vehicle after establishing a stable income source. Racing potential is most useful when the vehicle can be repaired and upgraded without exhausting the garage budget.
Expand the collection gradually and assign each vehicle a clear purpose. Keep versatile vehicles for everyday work and reserve specialized vehicles for activities where they perform best.

mechanicLegendsTuningEngine.title: Mechanic Legends Tuning and Engine Parts Guide
mechanicLegendsTuningEngine.subtitle: Tune Every Vehicle for the Way You Race: learn the core workshop flow for removing engine components, replacing parts, installing racing upgrades, and improving vehicle performance.
mechanicLegendsTuningEngine.intro: Vehicle performance is shaped by the parts you install and the way you balance speed, acceleration, handling, and control. Use the workshop to inspect the vehicle, replace worn or lower-performing components, install racing parts, and build a setup that matches your preferred driving style.

steps.title: Inspect the vehicle before changing parts
steps.description: Start by checking the vehicle and identifying the areas that need attention. A complete inspection helps separate repair work from performance upgrades and prevents unnecessary part changes.
actions: Enter the workshop with the vehicle you want to improve.
Review the available engine and vehicle components.
Identify damaged, missing, or lower-performance parts before beginning the upgrade.
steps.performanceFocus: Establishes a baseline for comparing later changes.

steps.title: Remove and replace engine components
steps.description: Engine work is handled component by component. Remove the selected part, install a replacement, and continue until the engine is restored or upgraded.
actions: Select the engine component that requires service.
Remove the existing part through the workshop interaction.
Install the replacement component and continue checking the remaining engine parts.
steps.performanceFocus: Restored components support consistent acceleration and top-speed performance.

steps.title: Install racing-oriented parts
steps.description: After the basic engine condition is addressed, use available racing components to focus the vehicle toward competitive driving.
actions: Choose performance parts that support the intended race type.
Prioritize engine upgrades for straight-line speed and acceleration.
Avoid sacrificing too much control when preparing for routes that require turning.
steps.performanceFocus: Performance parts are most effective when selected as a complete setup rather than as isolated upgrades.

steps.title: Balance speed, acceleration, and handling
steps.description: A fast vehicle is not always the quickest vehicle on every route. Match the tuning direction to the driving environment and your ability to control the car.
actions: Use a speed-focused setup for long straight sections and drag racing.
Use an acceleration-focused setup when quick launches and repeated starts matter.
Use a handling-focused setup for drifting, corners, and roads that require frequent correction.
steps.performanceFocus: Balanced builds are generally easier to control during exploration and mixed driving.

steps.title: Test the setup and refine it
steps.description: Take the vehicle onto the road after each major change. Testing reveals whether the upgrade improves the way you actually drive.
actions: Test launch response, acceleration, and top speed.
Check steering stability and control during turns.
Change one group of parts at a time so the effect of each adjustment is easier to understand.
steps.performanceFocus: Repeated testing turns workshop upgrades into a practical race setup.

mechanicLegendsJobsRepair.title: Mechanic Legends Jobs and Repair Guide
mechanicLegendsJobsRepair.subtitle: Choose Jobs That Build Skill and Income: understand the basic workflow for repairing damaged vehicles, completing deliveries, and handling taxi work.
mechanicLegendsJobsRepair.intro: Jobs provide structured ways to earn progress while learning the game systems. Repair work develops workshop familiarity, delivery work emphasizes consistent travel, and taxi work rewards efficient driving between destinations. Start with manageable tasks, learn the required interactions, and increase the difficulty as your vehicle and driving confidence improve.

items.title: Repair damaged vehicles
items.summary: Workshop-focused jobs require you to restore a damaged vehicle by identifying the required service and completing the repair process.
workflow: Accept or select the available repair job.
Bring the assigned vehicle into the workshop area.
Inspect the damaged components and complete the required repair interactions.
Finish the job and collect the reward after the vehicle is restored.
tips: Read the repair requirements before removing parts.
Work through the vehicle systematically instead of switching between unrelated components.
Use repair jobs to learn the workshop controls before investing heavily in performance tuning.
items.risk: The main risk is incomplete repair work or spending time on upgrades that are not required for the job.
items.rating: Recommended as a first job type

items.title: Complete delivery work
items.summary: Delivery jobs focus on transporting the required vehicle or cargo to a destination while maintaining an efficient route.
workflow: Select a delivery assignment and review its destination.
Prepare a vehicle that is steady and easy to control.
Drive to the destination while avoiding unnecessary detours and collisions.
Complete the handoff and receive the job reward.
tips: Use a controllable vehicle rather than choosing speed alone.
Learn the roads and common routes through repeated trips.
Avoid aggressive driving when a collision could slow down the delivery.
items.risk: Poor route choices, crashes, and loss of time can reduce the efficiency of the run.

items.title: Work as a taxi driver
items.summary: Taxi work centers on picking up passengers, driving to the requested destination, and completing the trip efficiently.
workflow: Locate and pick up the passenger.
Drive the passenger to the requested destination.
Complete the drop-off and collect the fare or job reward.
tips: Use a vehicle with predictable handling and steady acceleration.
Plan turns early and keep the passenger route as direct as possible.
Practice smooth driving to reduce delays caused by crashes or missed turns.
items.risk: Long detours, difficult vehicle control, and collisions can make the trip slower and less profitable.
items.rating: Recommended after becoming comfortable with navigation

items.title: Suggested beginner progression
items.summary: A simple progression is to learn repairs first, then move into deliveries and taxi work once basic driving and navigation are familiar.
workflow: Begin with repair jobs to understand vehicle condition and workshop interactions.
Move to delivery jobs to practice road travel and route planning.
Try taxi jobs after learning how to control the vehicle while following destinations.
Return to the most efficient job type when saving for vehicle improvements.
tips: Use early rewards to improve dependability and control before chasing maximum speed.
Choose jobs that match the vehicle you currently own.
Repeat the job type you can complete consistently rather than relying on risky runs.
items.risk: Taking difficult travel jobs before learning the route or vehicle controls can reduce completion efficiency.

mechanicLegendsDragRaceDrift.title: Mechanic Legends Drag Race and Drift Guide
mechanicLegendsDragRaceDrift.subtitle: Prepare the Right Car for Every Race: compare drag racing, drifting, road exploration, and multiplayer competition with practical preparation and driving advice.
mechanicLegendsDragRaceDrift.intro: Different activities reward different vehicle characteristics. Drag racing favors acceleration and straight-line speed, drifting requires controlled slides and predictable handling, while exploration and multiplayer events reward a setup that remains dependable across changing roads and opponents.

items.title: Drag racing
items.description: Drag races emphasize launch response, acceleration, and the ability to maintain speed over a mostly straight course.
bestSetup: Use a stable vehicle that can stay pointed straight during the launch.
Reduce unnecessary handling compromises when the route contains few turns.
drivingTips: Prepare the vehicle before entering the race.
Accelerate smoothly and keep corrections small.
Use the available straight-line space to maintain momentum.
items.idealFor: Players who prefer short, direct competitions and maximum straight-line performance.

items.title: Drifting
items.description: Drifting is based on controlling a slide through turns while maintaining direction, momentum, and recovery control.
bestSetup: Choose predictable handling over maximum top speed.
Use a vehicle that responds clearly to steering and throttle input.
Avoid a setup that becomes difficult to recover once the rear of the vehicle steps out.
drivingTips: Enter corners with enough speed to initiate a slide without losing control.
Use steering and acceleration together to maintain the drift angle.
Correct gradually and exit the corner with the vehicle pointed toward the next section.
items.idealFor: Players who enjoy technical driving, controlled slides, and corner-focused challenges.

items.title: Road exploration
items.description: Exploration rewards a dependable vehicle that can handle varied roads, navigation, and repeated travel between activities.
bestSetup: Choose dependability and control when learning the map or traveling between jobs.
Keep enough speed to travel efficiently without making every turn difficult.
drivingTips: Learn major roads and turns through repeated trips.
Use controlled braking before corners instead of relying on last-second corrections.
Treat exploration as a way to practice routes before entering competitive events.
items.idealFor: Players who want to discover the game world and build familiarity with travel routes.

items.title: Multiplayer races
items.description: Multiplayer competition combines vehicle preparation, race awareness, and the ability to adapt when other players create pressure or block a preferred line.
bestSetup: Select a vehicle that matches the race format rather than using one universal build.
Balance acceleration and handling when the route contains both straights and turns.
Test the setup before competing so you know how it reacts under pressure.
drivingTips: Choose a clean racing line and avoid unnecessary contact.
Use early braking and controlled exits to remain consistent around other players.
Adapt the setup after observing whether the race favors launches, corners, or sustained speed.
items.idealFor: Players who enjoy direct competition and comparing vehicle builds with other drivers.

mechanicLegendsUpdatesFeatures.title: Mechanic Legends Updates and Features
mechanicLegendsUpdatesFeatures.subtitle: Track the Features That Change Your Garage: use this overview to organize update information, vehicle additions, feature changes, and developer announcements from the official game pages.
mechanicLegendsUpdatesFeatures.intro: Updates can affect vehicles, workshop systems, jobs, races, and the overall driving experience. Check the official game page when a new version appears, then compare the current description with your previous setup so you can identify new content and adjust your garage routine.

items.whatToCheck: Look for newly available vehicles or changes to the vehicle selection.
items.playerImpact: A new vehicle can create additional options for drag racing, drifting, exploration, or job completion.
items.action: Test the vehicle in workshop and road activities before replacing an established build.

items.whatToCheck: Check for changes to engine work, part replacement, racing components, or vehicle performance systems.
items.playerImpact: Changes to parts or tuning can alter the balance between acceleration, speed, and handling.
items.action: Review existing vehicles after an update and retest their previous race setups.

items.whatToCheck: Review changes to repair work, delivery tasks, taxi activities, and job rewards.
items.playerImpact: Task order and preferred earning methods may change when job requirements or rewards are adjusted.
items.action: Compare completion time and reward value across available jobs before choosing a farming route.

items.whatToCheck: Look for new race options, drift activities, road content, or multiplayer changes.
items.playerImpact: New activities may favor different vehicle setups and driving techniques.
items.action: Prepare both a speed-focused build and a balanced handling build when the update adds new competition types.

items.whatToCheck: Review changes to controls, progression, garages, interaction flow, and general gameplay systems.
items.playerImpact: Small system changes can affect how quickly players accept jobs, repair vehicles, or access activities.
items.action: Repeat the basic workshop and job flow after updating so new interactions become familiar.

items.whatToCheck: Read the latest official description and announcement text available on the game pages.
items.playerImpact: Announcements provide the clearest overview of the intended focus of a new version.
items.action: Use the official game page as the starting point for identifying current features and version changes.

faq.title: Frequently Asked
faq.subtitle: Everything you need to know about Mechanic Legends

questions.question: What is Mechanic Legends?
questions.answer: Mechanic Legends is a free Roblox car repair and tuning simulator by Mechanic Devs. You repair damaged vehicles, dismantle engines, install performance parts, complete jobs, and take modified cars to drag races and drift events across 50+ vehicles.

questions.question: Is Mechanic Legends free to play?
questions.answer: Yes. Mechanic Legends is free to play on Roblox with optional in-game purchases, and it runs on PC, mobile, Xbox, and PlayStation.

questions.question: How do I redeem codes in Mechanic Legends?
questions.answer: Open Mechanic Legends, enter the garage or main interface, find the Codes option, type a code exactly as shown, and select Redeem. Codes can expire, so redeem them as soon as possible.

questions.question: How do I make money fast in Mechanic Legends?
questions.answer: Start with repair jobs for steady Cash, add deliveries once you know the roads, and move into taxi work and races as your vehicle improves. Reinvest earnings into parts that match the activity you play most.

questions.question: Which car should I buy first in Mechanic Legends?
questions.answer: Pick an affordable starter vehicle that leaves Cash for repairs, then add a work vehicle for deliveries and a performance car for races as your garage grows.

questions.question: Does Mechanic Legends keep getting updates?
questions.answer: Yes. Mechanic Legends receives updates with new cars, parts, features, and balance changes. Check the Updates and Features section on this wiki for the latest overview.
